speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to narrow down the cause of these neurological deficits, have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or drooping of your eyelids?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest, combined with double vision upon looking up or down, is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. REQUEST TEST: Anti-AchReceptor_Antibodies. REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.
